sections.name: Dull Bones
sections.card:
Summary: A chartreuse skeleton Koopa that throws bones and builds more Dull Bones to help it; it has 1 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense, and turns up commonly in Hooktail Castle.
Weak points: A Hammer swing takes one out easily, and a POW Block or Koops's Power Shell is very efficient against a crowd; unlike Dry Bones, they cannot put themselves back together once they are down.
Tips: They use Build to summon more Dull Bones, which is why Goombella says attacks that strike many at once are the most effective.
Tips: Besides Hooktail Castle they appear in the Glitz Pit, the Palace of Shadow and the Pit of 100 Trials, and they can drop a Dried Shroom, a Fright Mask or a POW Block.

sections.name: Iron Cleft
sections.card:
Summary: A large blue Cleft made of metal; the only ones are the two Iron Adonis Twins you face in the Glitz Pit, and each has 6 HP and charges for 4 damage.
Weak points: No attack damages them, not even moves that bypass defense or a perfectly timed Superguard; the only known way to hurt one is Yoshi's Gulp, which hits one Iron Cleft with the other.
Tips: Gulp is Yoshi Kid's move: he swallows an enemy and spits it at another enemy.
Tips: Goombella's Tattle says the only way to beat one is to whack it with the other, and that running away may not be a bad idea; the one in green shoes is the younger brother.

sections.name: Poison Pokey
sections.card:
Summary: A poisonous Pokey with 8 HP and 4 attack that can call in more of its kind; you meet it at Riverside Station and on floors 41 to 49 of the Pit of 100 Trials.
Weak points: Fire works well, since they are highly susceptible to burning, and the Tattle Log says to take it out quickly.
Tips: Slam, Body Throw and Bonk do 3, 4 and 5 damage and all poison you, its Pull move brings in another Poison Pokey, and poison slowly drains your HP.
Tips: A Poison Pokey sometimes drops a Tasty Tonic when it is beaten, which cures poison, and Goombella warns that it has spines all over, so do not touch them.

sections.name: Magnus von Grapple (Chapter 2 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The giant X-Naut robot that Lord Crump drives as the boss of Chapter 2, in the Great Tree; it has 30 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense.
Weak points: Its rocket fists are separate targets with 2 HP and no defense; it sends them out once its own HP reaches twenty, and Flurrie's Gale Force with a perfect action command is sure to remove them.
Tips: While the fists are out it can only jump and stomp the ground, hitting Mario and his partner for 2 piercing damage, which a floating Flurrie is not hurt by, and each fist hits for 4.
Tips: If both fists are beaten, a new pair is back by its second turn afterwards; after that it picks the stomp 60% of the time and releases the fists 40%, and any fists still out when its HP runs out are defeated at once.

sections.name: Doopliss (Chapter 4 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The Chapter 4 boss from the Creepy Steeple, fought three times with 40 HP each time and an attack of 4, then 4, then 6 in the Palace of Shadow.
Weak points: In the first fight he changes into a shadowy outline of Mario once his HP drops below 20, and even if you reduce him to zero before that, he changes anyway and is left with 10 HP.
Tips: Goombella cannot tattle his name, which shows as five question marks, and learning it later is what lets Mario hurt him; partner badges such as HP Plus P or Power Plus P are switched off in the second fight.
Tips: In the Palace of Shadow rematch he hits harder: his Head Missile does 6, and he copies Mario or one of your partners and attacks as them.

sections.name: Cortez (Chapter 5 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The pirate skeleton who holds the Sapphire Star in Pirate's Grotto on Keelhaul Key; he has three forms of 20 HP each, 4 attack and 1 defense, and he rises again in a new form when each of the first two falls.
Weak points: In his second, serpent form, hit the bone pile twice and he opens his rib cage to show a green gem; the gem has no defense and takes 1 extra damage from every attack.
Tips: In his last form the four weapons fight on their own; a strong attack that hits everything, such as a Thunder Rage or Vivian's Fiery Jinx, shuts them down for two turns, and Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them off the stage for good.
Tips: In the first form he swings four weapons and can hit one or both of you each turn, and the rusty hook can poison; at 10 HP or less in the last form he eats half the audience to heal, so a swift finish beats a long fight.

sections.name: Lord Crump (Keelhaul Key fight)
sections.card:
Summary: The third time you fight Lord Crump, at Keelhaul Key in Chapter 5, he brings a platoon of X-Nauts: 30 HP a round for two rounds, 3 attack and no defense.
Weak points: Goombella says that if you take out their leader, the X-Nauts lose the focus to attack, so go for Crump first.
Tips: He only body-slams for 3, heals after round one, and in round two summons replacements for the X-Naut platoon the turn after they fall; Goombella warns that the X-Nauts around him are a force to be reckoned with.

sections.name: Smorg (Chapter 6 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: A huge mass of small Smorgs that attacks on top of the Excess Express in Chapter 6, with 50 HP, 5 attack and 1 defense; it is the only chapter boss besides the Shadow Queen that guards no Crystal Star.
Weak points: Three tentacles (Smorg Miasmas) surround the body at the start, so defeat them first: in the GameCube game that drops the body's defense to 0, and in the Switch remake the body takes no damage until they are gone.
Tips: The tentacles regenerate, so Goombella says to use that time to deal heavy damage.
Tips: After it takes a lot of damage the tentacles change into a pincer claw that does 10 damage, against 5 for the Tentacle Slap.

sections.name: Magnus von Grapple 2.0 (Chapter 7 boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The upgraded robot Lord Crump drives in the X-Naut Fortress at the end of Chapter 7, with 70 HP, 6 attack and 2 defense; it is the last boss that holds a Crystal Star.
Weak points: Its X-Punch fists have 5 HP, 9 attack and no defense, Goombella says to take them down early, and Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them away.
Tips: Its main attack is a drill dive from above for 6 damage to Mario and his partner, and when its HP gets low it adds machine guns.
Tips: Its Rapid Fire Cannon sucks up audience members and fires them at whoever is in front for 10 hits of 3 damage, and while the fists are flying you may be hit by the fists and the body in one turn.

sections.name: Gloomtail (Palace of Shadow boss)
sections.card:
Summary: Hooktail's older brother, the dragon who guards the Star Stone in the Palace of Shadow, with 80 HP, 8 attack and 2 defense; he is stronger than his sister.
Weak points: He stores power with Charge Up (+8), which warns that the 16-damage Megabreath is coming, and Goombella says to use Vivian to hide from those attacks.
Tips: His poison breath lasts at least ten turns and he stomps or chomps whoever is in front for 8; Earthquake does 10 piercing damage but does not work on Vivian or Flurrie.
Tips: Beating him makes him cough up the chest holding the Star Stone, which unlocks the pedestals in the Palace of Shadow Tower.

sections.name: Grodus (Palace of Shadow boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The head of the X-Nauts, fought in the Palace of Shadow, with 50 HP, 7 attack and 1 defense; his defense rises by 1 for every Grodus X around him.
Weak points: He needs four Grodus Xs to raise a force field and destroying even one breaks it, and an attack on his scepter can stun it, which stops him attacking for a while.
Tips: He casts Thunderbolt (7), Flamethrower (6, burns), Ice Beam (5, freezes) and Clock Beam (stops you), the first three piercing, and he can also counterattack with Payback or turn Dodgy.
Tips: Smoke from his scepter marks a dud move that does no damage.

sections.name: Bonetail (Pit of 100 Trials boss)
sections.card:
Summary: The skeletal dragon at the bottom of the Pit of 100 Trials, with 200 HP, 8 attack and 2 defense, the most HP of any enemy; she is the strongest boss in the game, stronger even than the Shadow Queen.
Weak points: When her HP gets low she can recover 20 HP, at most twice, which adds up to 40 HP on top of her 200.
Tips: Her breaths do 8 damage and can freeze (blue), confuse (green, pink in the Switch remake), shrink (purple) or put you to sleep (white); guarding or Shell Shield avoids all of them.
Tips: Besides the breaths and Recover she only has Stomp and Chomp for 8, with none of Gloomtail's earthquake or Megabreath, and once beaten she coughs up the Return Postage badge and cannot be fought again.

sections.name: Star Pieces
sections.card:
Summary: Hidden collectibles: there are 100 Star Pieces in the game, 98 lying around the world and two given as rewards by Chef Shimi and the Excess Express waitress.
Uses: Trade them for badges with Dazzle in Rogueport Underground; all 100 are needed to get every badge he sells.
Tips: Dazzle's prices in Star Pieces: Attack FX Y 1, Chill Out 2, Pretty Lucky 3, Happy Flower, Happy Heart and Happy Heart P 4 each, Item Hog 5, Heart Finder and Flower Finder 6 each, Peekaboo 7, Quick Change 8, Flower Saver and Flower Saver P 10 each, Power Plus and Power Plus P 15 each.
Tips: Merluvlee will tell you where they are for five coins and Ms. Mowz can detect them as a field ability; buried ones need the Super Boots to flip their panel, and in the GameCube game the Ultra Hammer cannot.

sections.name: Partner ranks
sections.card:
Summary: A rank-up raises a partner's attack power and HP and teaches it a new move; there are two, Super Rank then Ultra Rank, and Merlon in Rogueport does each one for three Shine Sprites.
Uses: Super Rank teaches Goombella Multibonk, Koops Shell Shield, Flurrie Lip Lock, Yoshi Kid Mini-Egg, Vivian Fiery Jinx, Bobbery Hold Fast and Ms. Mowz Tease; Ultra Rank teaches Goombella Rally Wink (Mario gets a second turn), Koops Shell Slam, Flurrie Dodgy Fog, Yoshi Kid Stampede, Vivian Infatuate, Bobbery Bob-ombast and Ms. Mowz Smooch (heals Mario 10 HP).
Tips: Bobbery has the most HP at each rank (20, 30, then 40), and Koops has the lowest once ranked up (15 at Super, 25 at Ultra).
Tips: Ultra Rank needs the Up Arrow first: after you bring the Sapphire Star back to Rogueport, Merlon gives you a riddle, and the Up Arrow is in a secret room in Hooktail Castle behind a crack in the right wall of the room where you found the Black Key (Bobbery blasts it open, then hit the blue ! Block for the chest); give it to Merlon and he frees the Ultra Stone.

sections.name: Healing mushrooms
sections.card:
Summary: A Mushroom restores 5 HP, a Super Shroom 10 HP and an Ultra Shroom 50 HP, and since partners have HP now, they can heal a partner too.
Uses: A Life Shroom (called Life Mushroom in the Switch remake) revives Mario or his partner with 10 HP when they fall, and partners use it automatically as soon as their HP runs out, so you cannot save it for Mario alone.
Tips: Super Shrooms are sold at Westside Goods, the souvenir shop, Twilight Shop, Keelhaul Galleria, the Sales Stall and Northwinds Mart; Ultra Shrooms are rare, costing 200 coins at the Deepdown Depot, 67 Pianta tokens at the Pianta Parlor (80 in the Switch remake), or sometimes 120 coins from Charlieton.
Tips: You get a Life Shroom as the shopping prize at 150 shop points, an enemy may carry one and drop it after it is beaten, and Ms. Mowz can steal it with Kiss Thief.
